decisions: MIGRATIONS ARE COMMITTED THE MOMENT THE APPLY IS CONFIRMED. 0119 and 0120 were applied by the architect and committed immediately after I verified them against the live schema. The db-reset incident is the reason: the replay rebuilds from COMMITTED migration files, so an applied-but-uncommitted migration is precisely what a reset drops - that is how v_operations_by_driver_monthly was lost once.

THE APPLY WAS VERIFIED, NOT TAKEN ON REPORT. 0119: three demo columns gone, vin + utilization_pct kept, 15/13 rows unchanged. 0120: zero trucks% columns, 9 columns (was 13), no busy_trucks/truck_state in the viewdef, one row returned. Security: reloptions {security_invoker=true}, anon FALSE, authenticated TRUE, schema-wide 40/40/0. The anon check is the one that mattered - Supabase default privileges re-grant anon on every newly created relation and a REVOKE does not survive a DROP, so 0120's restated footer was enforcement rather than ceremony. It held.

EVERY DATE-KEY COMPARISON PUTS BOTH SIDES ON ONE CLOCK. toISOString().slice(0,10) is UTC; trip_date, expected_return_on and every other DATE column in this schema are local calendar terms. Mixing them is correct for 21 hours a day and wrong for the three after Riyadh midnight, which is exactly why four instances survived multiple review passes. There are now ZERO slice(0,10) date keys left in app/, lib/ and components/.

NO NEW DATE HELPERS. All four fixes route through todayKey()/daysAgoKey() in lib/utils.ts. today+7 is daysAgoKey(-7) - negative n is the existing helper's own arithmetic, not a new function - and it was proven under TZ=Asia/Riyadh across month and year rollovers (Aug 28 to Sep 4, Dec 28 to Jan 4, Feb 25 to Mar 4).

A SECOND PRIVATE COPY OF A DATE HELPER IS HOW THIS FAMILY SPREAD. PurchaseOrders.tsx's local daysAgoKey was logic-identical to the shared one and therefore harmless - and that is why it survived four passes. Removing it is deduplication, not a fix: the danger was the next person editing the local copy and the change never reaching the other three pages.

todayKey() IN A CLIENT COMPONENT IS ESTABLISHED CONVENTION HERE, not a new exposure - it was already used in eleven 'use client' modules before this sweep. Checked before changing StatementViews and PartsUsageTab rather than assumed.

context_notes: READ CLAUDE.md SECTION 7 FIRST - it is the durable record and this file is only a pointer to it. THE MONTH-KEY FAMILY, FOUND BUT NOT FIXED. The sweep for slice(0,10) turned up a slice(0,7) sibling with a WIDER blast radius, in money code, so it was flagged instead of fixed. lib/commission-rows.ts:93 - export const CURRENT_MONTH_KEY = new Date().toISOString().slice(0,7) - plus monthKeyOf(new Date().toISOString()) at app/trips/BreakdownReport.tsx:104, CustomersTab.tsx:139 and FinanceTab.tsx:327 (monthKeyOf itself is a pure slicer and is fine; the bug is the caller handing it a UTC string). TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS, and the second is the serious one. (1) UTC skew: on the FIRST of a month, 00:00-02:59 Riyadh, these report the PREVIOUS month. (2) CURRENT_MONTH_KEY IS A MODULE-LEVEL CONST, so it is evaluated once when the module first loads and never rolls over - stale for the whole lifetime of a client SPA session, and frozen at process start wherever it is evaluated server-side. IT IS NOT A DISPLAY VALUE: app/drivers/CommissionsTab.tsx uses it at lines 796, 887, 891 and 946 as the month_key WRITTEN with setCommissionBonus and two fd.set('month_key', ...) calls, so a bonus can be recorded against the wrong month. This was not fixed here for two reasons - it is commission money, and it was outside the three scoped fixes. THREE OTHER THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. (1) Remaining toISOString() uses in app/ and lib/ are TIMESTAMPS (terminated_at, decided_at, updated_at) and are legitimate - do not sweep them; only DATE KEYS were ever wrong. (2) v_fleet_state_now now reports 6 trucks with a driver where it reported 7 earlier in this session, and drivers_active moved 6 to 5. Neither migration touches assigned_driver_id, so this is ordinary operational use, not migration fallout - noted so it is not mistaken for one later. (3) BUILD ONLY VIA ./scripts/safe-build.sh - it exits non-zero if dev is live, which it did again this batch, so every build ran with --dist-dir .next-verify and dev on port 3002 was left untouched. next build also REWRITES tsconfig.json, so git checkout -- tsconfig.json afterwards.
